$comment: P68 round 12 (lane `cs`, D-C-AN-ENUMS-FIXED-UNDERLYING-TYPE-LOST-ITS-NAME-IN-THE-CONVERSIONS): two enumerations with FIXED underlying types (C23 6.7.2.2) cross a translation-unit boundary — a function taking one and a struct holding both, declared in main.c and defined in def.c, whose clause spells `enum E : long volatile` — C23 6.7.2.2 makes the underlying type the UNQUALIFIED version of what the clause names, so the two units declare one type. The whole-program merge re-interns every unit's types into one fresh host, and the enum record now keeps the underlying type it was DECLARED with through that re-interning; an enum's layout is its underlying KIND's, which the merge always kept, so every size, offset and value here must agree between the units. MEASURED 2026-09-24, these two files compiled, linked and RUN together on each reference separately: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 at -std=c2x and mingw-w64 13.2.0 at -std=c2x exit 42 with no diagnostic (their -std=c17 -pedantic-errors modes refuse the C23 syntax); MSVC 19.51 has no fixed underlying types and abstains. exit 42 = the call's 40 plus the tag, with the struct's size, the value's offset and the enums' sizes agreeing across the units.
